trust_and_untrusted_text:
**1. Vouch**
- A job starts only when the latest actor to add the queue label has triage or higher. That event's time is vouch_at (creation row 1).
- Untrusted text after vouch_at reaches workers only after a re-vouch: a `/flow-factory retry` from someone with triage access or higher, a terminal or in-session retry by the person, or the label re-added. A retry from triage access does nothing else (row 44t).
- **Trusted** means write access or higher, read from the repository permission endpoint (person_channels item 5), not from author_association.
- Editors come from GraphQL `editor`, `lastEditedAt` and `userContentEdits`, and from `renamed` events, for the title, the body and every comment in the spec-input set. An unknown editor counts as untrusted.
- An edit to a spec-input comment counts as trusted only when its editor is a trusted account. Any other editor makes untrusted_edit true, and row 51b parks the job until a re-vouch. An edit made with the person's token is a trusted edit (person_channels item 5). This covers an outsider editing their own reply after a retry re-vouched it: a re-vouched reply counts at the body it had at the re-vouch (row 8r).

**2. issue.md and issue_digest (`bin/_flow_factory_text.py`). They read one set.**

The **spec-input set** is:
- the title;
- the body;
- **needs-info answers:** replies posted after a needs-info marker that name or quote a needs-info question id (`NI-<k>`) and come from a trusted author. The issue author is trusted only with write access or higher. A reply from an author who is not trusted, the issue author included, joins the set only after a retry from someone with triage access or higher (row 8r).;
- answers given with `flow-factory.sh answer` in needs_info, kept in the job's answers file (row 8a);
- every comment by a trusted author whose first line is `/flow-factory spec`. The text after that line is spec input.

issue.md quotes and fences exactly that set:
- each line is prefixed `> ` inside `<<<UNTRUSTED_ISSUE_TITLE>>>`, `<<<UNTRUSTED_ISSUE_BODY>>>` and `<<<UNTRUSTED_ISSUE_COMMENT id=...>>>` fences;
- runs of three or more `<` or `>` are neutralised to U+2039 or U+203A (new code).

Every other comment is listed by author, date and length only. This covers trusted discussion such as status notes, thanks and links, a reply during needs_info that names no question id, engine-marked comments, and the other `/flow-factory` commands.

issue_digest = sha256 over the spec-input set: the title, the body, and the ids and bodies of those comments and answers. So:
- text that does not move the digest never reaches a worker, and text that reaches a worker always moves it;
- ordinary trusted discussion never parks a job and never sends it back to intake;
- an edit to a spec-input comment moves it, and an edit by anyone other than a trusted account is also an untrusted edit (item 1).

**baseline_digest** has one writer: row 66i, when the engine writes in/issue.md for an intake launch. Every row that enters intake sets baseline_pending, and row 66i clears it. Before the first intake launch, and while baseline_pending is set, issue_changed is false. A retry after an issue change or an untrusted edit goes back through intake (rows 44c and 44d), which records the new baseline. intake_inputs has one writer, row 6 (ACCEPT), and lists the comment ids intake read. Row 8 records the ids of the answers that sent the job back to intake in events.jsonl; they are already in the spec-input set.

A person who wants a comment to change the requirements prefixes it with `/flow-factory spec`. The needs-info template asks for replies that start with the question id. The ready, needs-info and spec-approval templates explain both.

**3. pr-feedback.md and review-context.env**
- pr-feedback.md holds the PR title and body, quoted, plus trusted or engine-posted inline comments, reviews and conversation comments with their ids. Everything else is metadata.
- review-context.env holds only the engine ledger.

**4. First reader.** The intake judge, which has no tools.

**5. Worker reads.** In factory mode, flow's own read sites take issue and PR text from `$FLOW_FACTORY_IO/in/`; factory_mode_in_commands lists the changed sites, including the Collect step of skills/feedback-resolution, which otherwise runs bin/flow-pr-feedback.sh and prints every comment and review body on the PR. That is the commands' behaviour, not a limit on the worker. Under option 2 of worker_github_access, a worker can still run `gh issue view --comments` or `gh pr view --comments` with the read-only token and read untrusted comments; only the prompts stop it, because a disallowed-prefix rule that blocked those would also block the `gh issue view --json state` and `gh pr view --json` reads flow makes. Under option 1, the stand-in refuses those reads. No PreToolUse read-guard is added, because bang-fenced blocks bypass PreToolUse. plan.md requires workers to read issue and PR text only from trust-filtered files. The user decided on 2026-11-12 not to run workers as a separate OS user, so this design records a departure from that rule: the prompts and the fenced in/ files are the only guard (residual_risks).

**6. Worker GitHub access.** worker_github_access gives the two options and chooses the read-only token (option 2); option 1, no credential, applies when the user does not create that token. Under either one, the launcher passes none of the person's GitHub tokens, though a worker can still read the person's token from the keychain (`gh auth token`). Raw gh reads remain possible under option 2 and are bounded only by the prompts and the disallowed `gh api` prefix.

**7. Commands in comments.** person_channels item 5 holds the rules: trusted authors only (write access, or triage for retry); posted after the factory's latest marker, except `spec`.

**Ready back to rework.** The directive was "ready to rework only on a trusted CHANGES_REQUESTED review". Row 37 implements it. Three other paths depart from it on purpose, and each is recorded as a departure in references/flow-factory.md and in residual_risks:
- **The `/flow-factory rework <text>` comment** (row 37b), posted by a trusted author after the ready marker. The plan's decision table records it as an exception. The engine opens the PR under the account gh is signed in as, and GitHub refuses a review that requests changes on one's own PR (P6). Without this comment, a maintainer of a single-maintainer repository could not send a ready PR back from GitHub.
- **The `flow-factory.sh rework <text>` subcommand** (row 37c), run by a person from a terminal, or through the interactive executor in default permission mode.
- **The `flow-factory.sh feedback` subcommand in ready** (row 37d), under the same conditions. It also moves a needs_human job to rework, spec or build (rows 45, 46 and 46b), which is not a departure, because those jobs are not ready.

All three undo ready first, set round_limit = round + maxRounds and put the text into pr-feedback.md. Plan Step 1.2 asks for the subcommand and feedback to be recorded next to the comment, which this item and residual_risks do.

**12. Outsiders on a public repository.**
- An open PR that says "Closes #N" blocks queueing (creation row 1) only when its author has write access or higher, so a fork PR cannot stop an issue from being queued.
- An issue closed by someone without write access, such as an outside issue author, parks the job in needs_human (row 53u). It does not cancel the job or close the factory PR. A person cancels, or reopens the issue and retries.
- The job's PR is the one the engine created, by its recorded number and with its head in this repository (stages item 6). A fork PR with the predictable `feature/issue-N-<slug>` branch name is never read as the job's PR.
- An outside issue author can still edit the issue after every retry, and each edit parks the job and stops a live worker (row 51b). A person stops this by locking the issue or by cancelling. residual_risks states it.
- Outside comments, CHANGES_REQUESTED reviews from outsiders, outside needs-info replies (row 8u) and markers from authors off the merge trust list are ignored.
- One kind of author without write access can still park a job: one on /flow:merge's association list (OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR by default), such as a read-only outside collaborator or an organisation member with no access to this repository. /flow:merge would trust their marker, so the factory parks rather than mark ready a PR whose ledger /flow:merge would misread (review_routing_and_markers item 5, which gives the ways out).

**8. Engine-posted model text.** `<!--` is neutralised except for the engine's own marker line and one validated cycle line. @mentions are put in backticks. A line of model text that starts with `/flow-factory` is put in backticks, and the engine's marker is always the first line of what it posts, so the command parser, which ignores every comment whose first line is an engine marker, never reads worker or judge text as a command. Length is capped at 60,000 characters.

**9. Settings views.**
- **User-only from the main checkout:** trust lists, routing, budgets, switches, the resolve policy and hold limits.
- **Base ref plus user:** gate, bootstrap, protected paths and risk areas.
- **Marker-trust list for agreement:** /flow:merge's own sources and order; see review_routing_and_markers item 5.

**10. Person-only channels.** Approvals and answers come only through the person subcommands, trusted comments, or the interactive executor in default permission mode, where tier-gate's ask is the confirmation. person_channels describes the refusal layers for workers and the checks for sessions. A deliberately detached same-user process can still evade the worker layers; this is a residual risk.

**11. No tamper hash.** A worker running as the same OS user could write job state; the design does not claim otherwise.
person_channels:
This section says who may act for a person, through which channel, and how the engine checks it.

**1. Subcommands of `bin/flow-factory.sh`, by who calls them**

| Group | Forms | Called by |
|---|---|---|
| Engine and executor | `next --executor interactive\|headless`, `status [--brief\|--json\|--intent <intent>]`, `wait --max-seconds <n>`, `run --once\|--until-idle\|--watch [--detach] [--no-merge] [--scheduled]`, `probe --platform\|--interactive\|--environment\|--launch-context\|--github-write --sandbox <owner/repo>`, `question <qid> --prompt` | a person's terminal, the interactive executor, the scheduled runner; `status --intent`, which only reads, also from tier-gate (item 3) |
| Runner setup | `runner start` (runs `run --watch --detach --no-merge`), `runner print-launchd`, `runner print-cron` | a person's terminal, or `/flow:factory runner start` |
| Internal | `launch <directive-id>`, `report <directive-id>` | `launch` from `next` only, for a directive it created and has not started; `report` only from the launcher pid in that directive's lease (execution_model, Launcher) |
| Worker | `context --mode`, `await <qid> --max-seconds <n>` | workers, through flow-ask-policy.sh, the changed bang-fenced blocks and the Blocking: yes loop |
| Person | `answer <qid> --choice <n> [--text <t>]` (in needs_spec_approval the qid is the round's SPEC-<k> and the text is the change request), `approve-spec <job> --spec-hash <h> [--head <sha>]` (`--head` is required when the approval comes from the gate, row 23b, and must name the current head H), `confirm <intent>`, `feedback <job> <text>`, `rework <job> <text>`, `retry <job>`, `reject <job>`, `cancel <job>`, `rebuild <job>` | a person, from a terminal or through the interactive executor |

`context --mode` is also run by ordinary flow commands outside the factory. With both factory variables unset, the shell wrapper answers it as off.

**A person event in a state where it does not occur.** Each person event acts only in the states that its occurs_in list in transitions.json names. Raised for a job in any other state, for example `reject` or `retry` on a job in ready, it is refused without a move: the subcommand exits 3 with `EVENT_REFUSED=<event> state=<state>`, and a trusted comment gets no reaction other than a status note naming the state.

**2. Workers cannot run person subcommands**

(a) **The engine refuses** every person subcommand with exit 4 and `PERSON_ONLY_REFUSED=<reason>` when FLOW_FACTORY_JOB, FLOW_FACTORY_DIRECTIVE or FLOW_FACTORY_IO is set in its environment, or when any ancestor pid, found by walking `ps -o ppid=`, equals a launcher pid or a child (claude) pid recorded in any job's live lease. It refuses the internal `launch` and `report` the same way when a live lease's claude pid is an ancestor, and it refuses `run`, `next` and `probe` the same way. The P13 launch-context check also applies to a run without `--scheduled`: `run` is refused when the caller's ancestry and session match neither a person-started runner (a controlling terminal, or `/flow:factory runner start` from one) nor the recorded scheduled job, so a detached run that no person started is refused. `probe --environment` re-records the interpreter and the worker-token write check only from a controlling terminal, after the person types `probe` on it.

(b) **tier-gate.sh** applies to any session whose hook environment has FLOW_FACTORY_JOB or FLOW_FACTORY_DIRECTIVE set, which means a worker. There it allows exactly two forms, `flow-factory.sh context --mode` and `flow-factory.sh await <qid> [--max-seconds <n>]`. It denies every other Bash command that names flow-factory.sh or _flow_factory.py. The hook reads its own process environment, which is claude's, not the command's, so `env -u` inside the command does not change it.

**The wrapped forms** are tested for every person subcommand in P2 and in e2e-factory-engine and e2e-factory-github: plain; `env -u VAR …`; `bash -c '…'`; `sh -c '…'`; `timeout N …`; `nohup …`; and `python3 <plugin>/bin/_flow_factory.py <subcommand>`.

**Residual.** Layer (b) matches on command text, so a command that builds the script name at run time passes it. Layer (a) can then be evaded by a process that clears the variables and detaches so that launchd becomes its parent and that imitates a person-started runner's context. In phase 2 such a process could act as the outside-session runner and merge. Closing this needs a separate OS user for workers, which the user decided on 2026-11-12 not to build. residual_risks states it.

**3. Sessions that are not workers**

tier-gate applies its factory rules only where the factory is in use (github_writes_and_tiers, tier-gate additions). For the always-ask subcommands (confirm, approve-spec, feedback, rework, retry, reject, cancel and rebuild) and for `answer` with `--text`, it reads `permission_mode` from its hook input:
- **Default mode:** it always asks. The ask shows the whole command with its arguments: for `confirm <intent>`, the stored literal command and its sha256, which tier-gate reads with the read-only `flow-factory.sh status --intent <intent>`; for `approve-spec`, the spec_hash, the head when the approval comes from the gate, and the spec file path; for `answer ... --text`, the text. This ask is the confirmation in a session.
- **Any other mode, auto included, or no mode in the hook input:** it denies the call with `run it in a terminal outside Claude Code: <command>`. The classifier does not decide a PreToolUse deny.

`answer` without `--text`, `next`, `wait`, `question`, `status` and `probe` are not tiered. That Claude Code passes `permission_mode` to PreToolUse hooks is not verified; P9 decides it, and without it tier-gate denies these calls in every session, so they run only from a terminal.

**4. How the engine checks that a person confirmed**

A person subcommand runs **inside a Claude session** when CLAUDECODE is set in its environment or a `claude` process is among its ancestors.
- **Inside a session.** The engine acts on an always-ask subcommand, and on `answer` with `--text`, only when the session's heartbeat record (interactive_executor, Presence) shows permission mode `default` and the interactive probe group is not stale. tier-gate's ask (item 3) is then the confirmation. In auto mode, when the mode is unknown, or while the probe group is stale, the engine refuses with exit 4 and `PERSON_CONFIRM_REQUIRED next: run <command> in a terminal`, and nothing changes. For the always-ask subcommands, rows 69a to 69h of transitions.json model this refusal through the fact unvouched_session_action. So in auto mode, confirm items and every always-ask subcommand are confirmed in a terminal, whatever P9 shows, and confirm-tier jobs park before launch (row 40b), as under the headless runner.
- **Free text.** The text of a needs-info `answer --text` and of a spec redraft (`answer SPEC-<k> --text`) joins the spec input. In auto mode it is given in a terminal or by a trusted comment, never by the session. In default mode the text the session passes is shown in tier-gate's ask before the call runs.
- **`answer --choice` from a session**, for a held worker question, is taken as the person's answer to the AskUserQuestion the session asked. The engine cannot tell whether the person or the model chose the option; residual_risks states it.

**Outside a session, a controlling terminal.** A process that clears CLAUDECODE and detaches is not inside a session by these tests, so the engine also checks the terminal path. Outside a session, every person subcommand opens `/dev/tty`, prints the job, the subcommand and its arguments, and reads the job id typed back. `confirm <intent>` first prints the stored literal command, recomputes its sha256 from the outbox file and compares it with the hash events.jsonl recorded when the intent was created; on a mismatch it refuses with `INTENT_CHANGED` and asks nothing. `approve-spec` first prints the spec_hash, the spec file path and, for an approval from the gate, the head and the diff summary. A process with no controlling terminal, such as one that detached with setsid or under launchd, cannot open `/dev/tty` and is refused with `PERSON_CONFIRM_REQUIRED`. On this Mac (2026-11-12), opening `/dev/tty` failed with ENXIO after `os.setsid()` and inside a Claude Code Bash tool call, and succeeded in a child of Python's `pty.fork()`. The cost is one typed word per terminal action. A process can still allocate a pseudo-terminal (`script`, `expect`) and type the confirmation itself; residual_risks states it.

**What this stops:** an auto-mode classifier approving a person action, because tier-gate denies these calls in every mode but default and the engine refuses them from a session whose recorded mode is not default.

**What it does not stop:** a command built at run time, which tier-gate's text match does not see, run from a session whose heartbeat record says default mode; a same-user process that writes a heartbeat record; and a session that switches from default to auto mode after its record was written, which only tier-gate's per-call check catches. residual_risks states each.

**The factory directory.** The engine is the only writer under `<main checkout>/<runtime dir>/factory/`. hooks/scripts/factory-state-guard.sh, a PreToolUse hook for Write, Edit and NotebookEdit, denies writes there. It exits at once and allows the write when FLOW_FACTORY_MAIN is unset and no factory directory exists at the top of the cwd's repository. In a worker session it resolves the directory from FLOW_FACTORY_MAIN, not from the cwd, because the cwd is the job clone. It allows the write when it cannot resolve the directory, because tier-gate and the engine's own checks remain. tier-gate denies Bash commands that name the resolved absolute factory directory (github_writes_and_tiers). Neither stops a path built at run time.

**Later phase: answer records.** A later phase may add a PostToolUse hook on AskUserQuestion that records the option a person selected for an action id the engine issued, so that the engine could accept a session's person action in any permission mode. Phase 1 does not build it, and that Claude Code passes the answer to a PostToolUse hook is not verified. If it is built, the question the engine issues must contain what is approved: for a confirm, the stored literal command and its hash; for approve-spec, the spec_hash, the head when the approval comes from the gate, and the spec file path.

**5. Commands in comments**

- **Trusted means write access.** `/flow-factory answer|approve-spec|rework|reject|cancel|spec`, on the first line of an issue or PR comment, counts only when its author's permission on the repository is write, maintain or admin. The engine reads it from `GET repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{login}/permission` (`role_name`), caches it for one sync, and treats a failed read as untrusted. **Bot and App actors.** An actor whose login ends in `[bot]`, or whose type is Bot, is untrusted for vouching (the queue label), comments, reviews and cancel (removing the label or closing the issue), unless the user-only `trustedBots` list names it. For a listed bot the engine still reads its permission from that endpoint; P8 records what the endpoint returns for a bot login. `/flow-factory retry`, which re-vouches untrusted text, counts from triage or higher, but only as a re-vouch (below), because the plan's decision is that a reply from someone without write access counts once someone with triage access or higher confirms it. author_association is not used here: OWNER, MEMBER and COLLABORATOR do not imply write or triage access (an outside collaborator can have read access only, and an organisation member can have none on this repository). That the endpoint returns `role_name` triage for a triage user is not verified; P8 decides it, and without it a triage user counts as read access. The user-only `trustedPermission` (default `write`) may raise the bar to maintain or admin, never lower it.
- **Triage access counts only to re-vouch.** A `/flow-factory retry` from triage access, not write, re-vouches text from someone without write access: in needs_info it makes such needs-info replies count (row 8r), and in needs_human it re-vouches an untrusted edit (row 44d). It resumes no other park (row 44t, fact retry_by_triage_only).
- **Cancel by label.** Removing the queue label cancels the job only when the actor who removed it has write access or higher, the same bar as an issue close (fact cancel_signal, row 53b). A removal by a triage user or a bot posts a status note, re-adds nothing, and the job keeps running.
- The comment must also be posted after the factory's latest marker, except `spec`, which counts at any time. feedback, confirm and rebuild have no comment form.
- **`approve-spec` names the hash, and the head for a gate approval.** The comment form is `/flow-factory approve-spec <spec-hash> [<head>]`, with at least the first 12 hex digits of the spec_hash that the latest spec-approval notice prints. When the approval comes from the gate (row 23b), the comment must also name the current head H, at least its first 12 hex digits, which the notice prints; row 15s refuses an approval whose head is not the current H. When a push changes the spec while the job waits, row 52s posts a new notice with the new hash, so an approval posted before it no longer counts, and one that names the old hash is refused (row 15s).
- **Comments and other writes made with the person's credential (accepted risk).** The user decided on 2026-11-12 to accept this risk. No rule holds comments posted with an account gh on this machine is signed in as, and workers do not run as a separate OS user. Checked 2026-11-12 on this Mac: with GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN unset, `gh auth token` still prints the person's keyring token, with scopes repo, workflow, delete_repo, gist and read:org. So any same-user process, a worker included, can reach the person's write token whichever worker token option is chosen. A worker, or any Claude session running as the person, the interactive executor in auto mode included, can therefore act as the person on GitHub:
  - post a `/flow-factory` command, a `/flow-factory spec` comment or a needs-info answer, which counts as the person's, and post reviews as the person;
  - add labels; the queue label added with the person's token vouches a job (creation row 1);
  - edit titles, bodies and comments; such an edit is a trusted edit, so a title or body edit moves issue_digest and sends the job back through intake before build (row 50) or parks it for a retry after it (row 51);
  - close or merge the issue or the PR; the engine records such a close as a cancel (rows 53b and 53c) and such a merge as merged by the person (row 54), because GitHub reports the person's account.

  The engine cannot tell these from the person's own actions. tier-gate's deny of Bash comment posts that name `/flow-factory` stops ordinary tool calls only (github_writes_and_tiers). A credential for another GitHub account stored outside gh, for example in a git credential helper entry or a token file, can be used the same way. Under auto-merge a comment posted as the person could lead to a merge, so phase 2 shows this risk to the user again before the switch can be turned on (phasing). residual_risks states it.
- **Untrusted command comments** are ignored and listed by author, date and length only.

**7. Answers in the questions store**

The questions store is `<runtime dir>/questions/` in the job's worktree, which the worker can write: `flow-question.sh answer <id> --choice <n>` records `answered_by: person` unless `--by` says otherwise (flow-question.sh:334-348). The engine therefore never takes a store answer as a person's. That includes the conflict answers given to a later resolve launch, which the engine builds from its own events only (stages item 11).
- Every person answer is a person_answer event in events.jsonl, with its channel. The engine writes it to the store itself (row 67c, or the stage relaunch after row 44).
- `await` prints `ANSWERED` only when the store answer equals the engine's recorded event for that question.
- A post-stage check: every `Blocking: yes` question the stage stored has an engine-recorded answer. A store answer with no engine event fails the stage (stage_failed).
- The ready summary builds its answered list from engine events. It lists a store answer with no engine event as "answered in the worktree, not by a person", and phase 2 counts it as an unverified item. Soft drafts answered `--by recommendation` (specification-capture Step 3) are listed as decisions taken on a recommendation, as before.

**6. Recorded channels**

Each person action records in events.jsonl its channel (`terminal`, `comment:<id>` or `session:<session id>`) and the caller's ancestry. The ready summary lists the channel of every approval and answer.
worker_github_access:
**The problem**

Workers make no GitHub writes by design, but they run in the person's environment. If the launcher passes GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, the gh config directory and SSH_AUTH_SOCK on, a worker holds the person's write credential. The disallowed Bash prefixes (`gh api`, `gh issue …`, `gh pr …`, `git push`) do not cover curl or Python, so a worker could post a trusted `/flow-factory approve-spec` comment as the person.

Neither option below closes the comment channel, because a worker can read the person's keyring write token with `gh auth token` (below). The user decided on 2026-11-12 to accept that risk (person_channels item 5, residual_risks). The options differ in what else a worker can do with GitHub, and in what they cost. The plan leaves the choice between them to this design, and the design chooses **option 2** (below). Option 2 needs a read-only token that the user creates. If the user does not create one, or the organisation forbids such tokens, option 1 applies. Phasing asks the user for the token in phase 0, before P1 and P3 run, because both probes run the option that applies.

**What stays the same under both options**
- The launcher passes none of GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN, GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN, GIT_ASKPASS, GIT_SSH or GIT_SSH_COMMAND from the person's environment. GH_CONFIG_DIR and XDG_CONFIG_HOME point at an empty per-job directory under the worker area, so `gh api` and the other API commands in the worker find no login. `gh auth token` is different: with GH_CONFIG_DIR empty it can still read the person's keychain entry for the host and print the token (reported for gh 2.101.0 on 2026-11-11; P3 records it for the installed gh). So under either option the person's write token is one command away from a worker.
- GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL points at a per-job file that the engine generates. It holds user.name, user.email and the signing settings copied from the person's global config. It first sets `credential.helper` to empty, which clears every inherited helper; under option 1 nothing follows, and under option 2 the next line adds `!gh auth git-credential`, which answers with the read-only token in GH_TOKEN.
- The engine fetches origin into the main checkout before every worker launch and before every gate, then into the job clone, so the worktree sees current remote refs without a worker fetch. It fetches with `git fetch --no-write-fetch-head` (git 2.55.0 lists the option), so it never changes the main checkout's FETCH_HEAD under a person's own /flow:review, and it retries after one second when a remote-ref lock is held. Base-branch settings are read from the main checkout's refs, never from the job clone's.
- Signing: a GPG key (GNUPGHOME kept) signs without giving GitHub access. An SSH signing key held by the agent needs SSH_AUTH_SOCK, and the agent also authenticates `git push` over SSH. When the repository's signing setup needs the agent, the factory refuses to start workers and names the cause. The user can then sign with a GPG key, or with an SSH key file that `gpg.ssh.program` reads without the agent. P3 records which case applies. On this Mac, `git config --global` sets no commit signing (read 2026-11-11).
- Checked 2026-11-12 on this Mac: with GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN unset, `gh auth token` still prints the person's keyring token, with scopes repo, workflow, delete_repo, gist and read:org. So any same-user process, a worker included, can reach the person's write token whichever worker token option is chosen. Neither option closes the comment channel; the user accepted this on 2026-11-12 (residual_risks).
- A same-user process can still reach the person's stored credentials, for example with `gh auth token`, by running gh with the real config directory, or by asking a git credential helper. Neither option prevents that. With the token, a worker can post comments, add the queue label to any issue (which vouches a job, creation row 1), push, and merge wherever the repository allows. Nothing in the design stops it for comments, labels, edits or closes; the user accepted that risk on 2026-11-12 (person_channels item 5, residual_risks). For pushes and merges, GitHub rulesets that require a pull request and status checks on the default branch are the boundary: `probe --environment` reads the rules API, and status and `/flow:factory setup` warn when the default branch has neither a ruleset nor branch protection that requires them. residual_risks states the rest.

**Option 1: workers get no GitHub credential, and the engine does every GitHub read**

Every gh call and every network git call a worker makes then fails. These sites need factory-mode replacements. Among the scripts in plugins/flow/bin at aab0d132, bin/flow-pr-feedback.sh, run by the feedback-resolution skill, is the only one whose gh calls print comment or review text; it is in the table. P1 records any other call. A line already replaced in factory_mode_in_commands is marked "already replaced".

The replacement mechanism for option 1:
- **in/gh-facts.env**, written by the engine before each launch: REPO, DEFAULT_BRANCH, ISSUE_STATE, PR_NUM, PR_HEAD_OID, PR_BASE_REF, PR_BASE_OID and LINKED_ISSUE. Each "in/gh-facts.env" site reads it in factory mode.
- **A read-only gh stand-in** (`bin/factory-gh`, placed first on the worker PATH under the name `gh`). It answers only the read shapes in the table above, from JSON files the engine writes to in/gh/ before launch, and applies `--jq` filters with jq. Any other call prints `FACTORY_GH_REFUSED <argv>` and exits 1. Every call is logged. gh's `--jq` uses a different implementation from jq, so the e2e-factory-mode suite runs each filter in the table against both.
- **Skips** for `gh auth status`, `git ls-remote` and `git fetch` in factory mode.
- **P1 under option 1.** In phase 0 the stand-in does not exist yet, so P1 runs the four commands with no credential and records in probes.json every gh call and network git call that failed. That list is the work list for phase 1d, which builds the stand-in and the replacements. P1 is run again when 1d closes, with the stand-in on PATH, and its go condition is then an empty list.

**Option 2: workers get a read-only fine-grained token that the user creates**
- The user creates a fine-grained personal access token limited to the target repository, with read-only Contents, Issues, Pull requests and Metadata. The user puts it in an environment variable and names that variable in the user-only `worker.ghTokenEnv`. The launcher sets GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN in the worker to that value.
- Every gh read in the table above then works unchanged, and every write fails with 403. Worker `git fetch` over HTTPS uses `credential.helper=!gh auth git-credential` in the generated global config. Over SSH it has no key, which does not matter, because the engine has already fetched.
- The factory refuses to launch a worker while `worker.ghTokenEnv` is unset or empty, or while the token can write.
- **The write check** (P3, environment group) sends one write per permission with the worker token. Each request is built to be refused even when the token has the permission:
  - Issues: `POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/labels` with an empty name;
  - Pull requests: `POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls` with no head or base;
  - Contents: `PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/<path>` with no content.

  The expected answer is 403 for each. A 422 means the token had the permission and only the invalid body was refused, and the factory then refuses to start workers. That GitHub checks permission before it validates the body, so the two codes tell these cases apart, is not verified; P3 decides it. If the codes do not separate the cases, the check fails closed and workers do not start.
- When the token expires, this check fails. Worker launches then stop, with the status line in phasing (environment group).
- An organisation may require approval for fine-grained tokens, or forbid them. In that case option 2 is not available.

**Chosen: option 2.**
- It needs no gh stand-in and no edits to the read sites in the table above, and flow's commands run the reads they already make.
- Neither option stops a worker that deliberately reads the person's stored credential (`gh auth token` is enough). The user accepted that risk on 2026-11-12 (residual_risks).
- Neither option enforces what plan.md asks, that workers read issue and PR text only from trust-filtered files. Under option 2 a worker can read untrusted comments with the read-only token. Under option 1 the stand-in refuses `--comments` reads, but a worker can still run the real gh by its path with the token `gh auth token` prints. Only the prompts stop it (trust_and_untrusted_text item 5). The user decided on 2026-11-12 not to run workers as a separate OS user, so this is a recorded departure from plan.md (trust_and_untrusted_text item 5).
- Option 1 applies when the user cannot or does not want to create and renew a token, at the cost of the stand-in and the replacement list.

**Gate (`_flow_factory_gate.py`, engine directive, cwd = worktree)**

The gate runs with the recorded interpreter by absolute path, so a `.python-version` file in the worktree does not choose it.

**1. Settings**

`gate.commands` is read through `cascade-resolve.sh --repo-settings-ref origin/<base>` (git show, never a local file), plus the user tier. The ref is the main checkout's, after the engine's own fetch before every gate, never a ref in the job clone, so a worker's `git update-ref` cannot choose it. The timeout is the larger of the two sources. When the list is empty or unreadable, the gate parks the job in needs_human with reason gate_commands_missing (row 25e); `/flow:factory setup` and status warn about an empty list before any job reaches the gate.

**2. Protected and config-loading sets**

The protected set is the plugin default plus the base-ref list plus the user list. The plugin default covers:
- `.claude/**`, `.mcp.json`, `**/CLAUDE.md`, `**/CLAUDE.local.md`, AGENTS.md;
- `.flow/workflows/**`, `.flow/triggers/**`;
- `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/actions/**`, CODEOWNERS;
- every file under `<runtime dir>/goals/`;
- the scripts gate.commands and bootstrap.commands name.

The config-loading set is `.claude/settings*.json`, `.claude/{commands,agents,skills,hooks,rules,output-styles}/**`, `.mcp.json`, `**/CLAUDE.md`, `**/CLAUDE.local.md`, `.flow/workflows/**` and `.flow/triggers/**`.

**3. Protected check (at gate, before every worker launch, and right before every engine push)**

Let M = merge-base(HEAD, origin/<base>).
- **Tracked changes.** Any addition, modification, deletion or rename under a protected or config-loading path in `git diff --name-status M` is a violation. Two exceptions: the job's own goal file when it is new or equal to goal_freeze, and content equal to origin/<base>.
- **Untracked or ignored files.** `git status --porcelain -z --ignored --untracked-files=all`: any file under a config-loading path is a violation. That includes `.claude/settings.local.json` and `.claude/settings.flow.local.json`.
- **Allowlist.** Non-config `.claude` paths that P2 records, and the lock files covered by the prepare ignore rules, which are not under config-loading paths.
- **Result:** `protected`, and the job goes to needs_human.
- **Before a push.** The check and the clone config comparison run on the commits about to be pushed, right before every engine push (open_pr, review, rework, sync, resolve, and a held push released at waiting_operator). A violation freezes the job with nothing pushed: row 21f moves it to needs_human, and at waiting_operator rows 41 and 41k do not run the held push, so the job resumes into the recorded stage and the replayed stage result meets row 21f. So a workflow file a worker committed with Bash never reaches the remote, where GitHub Actions would run it with the repository's secrets.

**4. Running the commands**

In the worktree, with a cleaned environment (no GH tokens, the slot's PORT). Python enforces the timeout on the process group.

**5. Goal commands are written by the branch**

The gate does not run them. gate.json records them as advisory "branch-written checks".

The plain statement in the ready summary and the PR body: **the only check the branch cannot change is the base-ref gate.commands.** In phase 2 this blocks auto-merge, unless the goal's criteria equal the approved `## Factory criteria`.

**6. Goal freeze**

A sha256 is recorded after build. A later change gives `protected`.

**7. Diff risk**

flow-risk-check.sh runs with base-ref settings over merge-base..H. High risk with no approval goes to row 23b.

**8. Output: `round-k/gate-<H>.json`**

head_sha, base_sha, merge_base, gate_def_ref, interpreter, commands, protected_violations, goal_status, goal_hash_ok, diff_risk, result.

**Review carry-over**

A review carries to a merge commit H2 when all of these hold:
- H2's parents are (H, B);
- the merge was a clean engine merge;
- H2 adds no categories.

The ids are recorded as `carried_to`.

**Commit binding (factory records only)**
- **Gate:** gate.head_sha == HEAD == remote == headRefOid.
- **Review ledger:** head_start, head_end, carried_to, and each marker id with its SHA.
- **Phase 2:** approve-<H>.json and `--match-head-commit <H>`.
- **Base:** base_sha == the current base at ready and at merge.
- **Head changes:** a head change not made by a factory push goes to row 52 (row 52e before open_pr; rows 52s, 52h, 52hs, 52w and 52wp in the parked states). Each row that moves the branch first snapshots the old tip and a dirty worktree.

Nothing is added to the FlowGoal lifecycle, and /flow:merge is unchanged.

**Diff categories (`_flow_factory_categories.py`)**

They run over merge-base..H. Each list is the built-in rules plus the base-ref list plus the user list.

| Category | What triggers it |
|---|---|
| ci | CI configuration |
| deploy | deploy configuration |
| auth | auth path segments plus authPaths |
| migration | flow-contract-files.sh plus migration globs |
| dependency | only DEP_ADDED, DEP_CHANGED, DEP_INSTALL_HOOK and DEP_REPLACED from flow-dep-diff.sh |
| protected | the protected-path set |
| codeowners | CODEOWNERS |
| flow-config | flow's own configuration |
| gate-config | package scripts, Makefile, test configuration, files gate.commands names |
| riskarea | RISK=high with base-ref settings |

A helper result of `unavailable` counts as a hit in phase 2.

**Route (`round-k/route.env`)**
- **Inputs:** effective risk, surfaces, categories and `review.routing.*` (user-only).
- **Rules:**
  - security-reviewer and holdout-validation are always included;
  - low risk uses cheaper models;
  - high risk adds the grounding critic;
  - a ui surface adds integration-verifier;
  - a security surface, or an auth or dependency category, gives the security reviewer the strongest model, run twice.
- **Fallback (P1):** routing changes only the reviewer set.

**Markers**

**1. Kinds**

| Marker | Kind | Posted by the engine through | Read from |
|---|---|---|---|
| FLOW_REVIEW_CYCLE | PR review body | `gh api POST repos/O/R/pulls/N/reviews` with event COMMENT (returns the id) | pulls/N/reviews |
| FLOW_RESOLUTION_CYCLE | issue comment | `gh api POST repos/O/R/issues/N/comments` (returns the id) | issues/N/comments |

The idempotency lookup lists the same endpoints and matches the engine's `FLOW_FACTORY ... event=<id>` line.

**2. Who posts them**

The engine posts both. Each is recorded in round-k/ledger.json with its stage, round, head SHA, id, and the sha256 of the body it posted. P6 checks own-PR COMMENT reviews before 1f is built.

**3. Cycle numbers**
- MARKER_CYCLE is the count of engine-posted review markers + 1.
- ROUTE_CYCLE is 1.
- address's REVIEW_CYCLE is the number of factory rounds.
- No foreign post moves any of them.

**4. The factory ledger passes when all of these hold**
- the latest engine-posted review marker belongs to the current round and is valid at H;
- each of its findings is RESOLVED by a later engine-posted resolution marker from review or rework;
- ESCALATED is empty.

**5. Agreement with /flow:merge**

**How /flow:merge selects markers and resolves its trust list** (commands/merge.md, read at 601b78ec, where plugins/flow is unchanged from aab0d132):
- **Sources, first valid value wins (:264-349).** The loop at :299 reads, in this order:
  1. `.claude/settings.flow.local.json`;
  2. `.claude/settings.flow.json`;
  3. the user settings file named by `cascade-resolve.sh --user-settings-path`;
  4. `<install>/settings.json`.

  The two repository files are read at the top of the working tree merge runs in, as named by `cascade-resolve.sh --project-settings-path` (:298). `<install>` is the USER_FILES install outside the repository (:285-287). With no install outside the repository, only the two repository files are read.
- **Per source.**
  - A missing file is skipped.
  - A jq parse error prints `WARN: failed to parse …; skipping this source` and goes on to the next source (:308).
  - A missing or null `merge.markerTrust.allowedAssociations` is skipped.
  - A value that is not a non-empty array of strings prints `LEDGER_WARN: invalid markerTrust configuration …; falling through` (:334).
  - The first valid value is the list (:325).
  - If no source gives one, the list is `["OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR"]` (:275).
  - Values outside GitHub's association vocabulary, and high-risk values (NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR, MANNEQUIN), only warn.
- **Marker selection.** Every page of `repos/O/R/issues/N/comments` (:362) and of `repos/O/R/pulls/N/reviews` (:374) is read. A marker is a body matching `<!-- FLOW_RESOLUTION_CYCLE:[0-9]+ ` or `<!-- FLOW_REVIEW_CYCLE:[0-9]+ `, and it counts when its author_association is an exact member of the list (:365, :377). The last trusted marker of each kind is the one merge reads.
- **Failures.**
  - A gh failure blocks the merge (:384).
  - A jq failure while filtering blocks it (:394).
  - Markers that exist only from untrusted authors block it (:410, :413).

**What the factory does.** It resolves the list with the same four sources, in the same order, with the same per-source behaviour and the same default.
- It reads the two repository files at the top of the main checkout, the checkout the engine runs from.
- It takes the user file and the plugin file from the pinned `<install>`, through the same cascade-resolve.sh calls.
- A parse error or a wrong shape skips that source with merge's warning text in runner.log, and the next source is read.
- It never reads the job's worktree.

It selects markers from the same two endpoints, with the same pattern and the same exact-match trust filter.
- The list decides only which markers /flow:merge would count.
- The marker-agreement rule then requires that, among those markers, the latest of each kind is engine-posted, matched by the ids recorded in the ledger, and that its current body still has the sha256 recorded when the engine posted it. /flow:merge reads the body of the last trusted marker (merge.md:362-413), and a comment or review body can be edited after posting, by its author's account or by a maintainer, so an id match alone is not enough. If either check fails, a ready job parks (row 38), and a job in sync with the base unchanged parks (row 31b).
- Markers from authors off the list are ignored, as /flow:merge ignores them. So an outsider's `<!-- FLOW_RESOLUTION_CYCLE:N ` comment on a public repository does not park a ready job, whatever a source's parse state.
- The list is by author_association, and an association on it does not imply write access: with the default list, a read-only outside collaborator or an organisation member with no access to this repository can post a marker that /flow:merge would trust. The factory parks on it too (rows 38 and 31b), because /flow:merge would read that marker as the latest. The park ends in one of two ways, and status names both:
  - the foreign marker is deleted, or edited so it no longer matches the marker pattern, and a person retries (row 44r re-enters sync; while the foreign marker is still the latest trusted one, row 31b parks again);
  - a person gives feedback (row 45), and the round that follows posts engine markers that are the latest again.
- A gh or jq failure while reading markers fails the sync stage (stage_failed: rows 39 and 43a), as merge fails closed. It does not count as disagreement.
- If the resolved list includes high-risk values, status prints merge's warning.

**Remaining differences, and what the factory does about them.** The factory and a person's /flow:merge resolve the list the same way only when they read the same files. Three inputs can differ:
- **The checkout.** /flow:merge reads the repository files of whichever checkout the person runs it in. The factory always reads the main checkout's, because the job's worktree is written by a worker and must not choose whose markers count. When a person runs /flow:merge in another worktree whose settings files differ, the two lists can differ.
- **The install.** merge.md takes the plugin tier and the resolver from the first install in its candidate list (:285-287): `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` when set, then the newest cache version, then the marketplace copy. A person's session usually sets `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`; a launchd runner does not.
- **The user tier.** cascade-resolve.sh takes the user file from `FLOW_USER_SETTINGS` when the caller's environment sets it (:599-607), and otherwise from `<home>/.claude/settings.flow.json`.

`/flow:factory setup` therefore records, from the person's own terminal environment, the install path and the user settings path that merge.md's lookup resolves there. The factory reads exactly those two paths, whatever its own environment holds. status and runner.log warn when the runner's own lookup would resolve a different install or user file, and when the recorded install no longer exists. The checkout difference remains, and residual_risks states it.

**6. Rework resolution markers**

They count toward the round whose findings they resolve. Rework always leads to gate and then a new review at the new head (rows 30, 22).

**Two locations**

1. **Job state:** `<main checkout>/<runtime dir>/factory/`, with its own `.gitignore` of `*`.
   - Contents: .lock, state.json, probes.json, runner.lock, runner.log, executors/ and jobs/issue-N/.
   - The path depends on flow.runtime.stateDir and journal.dir, which a pull request can change. `/flow:factory setup` and `probe --environment` record the resolved absolute factory path in probes.json. The engine and the hooks use the recorded path, and the engine refuses with `FACTORY_REFUSED=factory_path_changed` when the settings later resolve to a different one, so a merged PR cannot move the factory directory away from running jobs, leases and records.
   - Each job folder holds: job.json, events.jsonl, outbox/, issue.md, intake-k.json, spec/, directives/, results/, round-k/, questions/ (a copy at terminal), feedback-k.md, approve-<sha>.json and rejection.md.
2. **Worker area:** `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/flow-factory/<owner>_<repo>-<hash>/`, outside the repository and outside ~/.claude.
   - Contents: worktrees/issue-N/ (the job clone, stages item 3), jobs/issue-N/state/ (the per-job FLOW_STATE_DIR) and jobs/issue-N/io/{in,out}.
   - It is not under `<flow state dir>` (default ~/.claude/flow-state, cascade-resolve.sh:555) because Claude Code treats files under .claude specially. claude 2.1.322 help describes person-only approval for writes to settings, git and tool-configuration files in restricted mode. Nobody has checked whether Edit and Write under acceptEdits with --permission-prompts none are refused there.
   - The user-only `worktreeRoot` may move the area, but it is refused under `$HOME/.claude` or `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.
   - P1 runs with the worktree at this real default location.

**Keeping the worktree clean**
- io is outside the worktree.
- runs/.gitignore is written at prepare.
- The clone's info/exclude gets the lock, auto-log and watch patterns (stages item 3).
- .flow/questions ignores itself.
- The finalize commit clears journal and goal changes.
- P1 records every path a stage run leaves in a scratch repository with an empty .gitignore. Any non-config path it finds joins the exclude list.

**/flow:setup changes for future repositories:** setup.md:130 and flow-runtime-state.md:28-40 add `<journal dir>/*.lock` and `<runtime dir>/goals/*.lock`.

**Per-job FLOW_STATE_DIR**

It isolates the goal trust ledger, quality ledgers, tier records, Stop-hook counters and session-end and System One data per job. The path is absolute and outside the repository (cascade-resolve.sh:102-125, carried).

**Ports**
- Slot s gets `PORT = base + step*s` (5100, 10) plus the next two ports.
- runtime-verification, visual-verification and integration-verifier use only those ports and stop only their own pid.
- COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME and FLOW_FACTORY_SLOT are also set.
- Build caches are not isolated.

**Bootstrap (engine directive)**
1. `bootstrap.commands` from the base ref plus the user tier, run with a timeout.
2. `bootstrap.copy`, refusing symlinks, paths outside the repository, protected or config paths, and files that are not ignored.
3. `rerunOn` globs.
4. The guard: a clean tree.

Bootstrap, at prepare and on a `rerunOn` re-bootstrap, runs with the same cleaned environment as the gate: no GH tokens, no SSH_AUTH_SOCK, the slot's PORT, and the worker keep list (execution_model), because rerunOn runs install hooks that the branch can change.

**Auth**
- **Workers** get the environment in execution_model, with GitHub access as worker_github_access sets it. They make no GitHub writes by design, and the launcher passes them none of the person's GitHub tokens, though a worker can still read one from the keychain (worker_github_access).
- **The engine** uses the person's auth and the real binaries (the `_tr_real` rule). It unsets FLOW_TIER_DIR and FLOW_TIER_CALL.

**Engine git commands**

A worker can run git, and git reads its configuration from the repository it runs in. Keys such as core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath, credential.helper, url.<x>.insteadOf, remote.<name>.pushurl and core.sshCommand make git run a program or send to another address. The engine therefore:
- gives each job its own clone (stages item 3), so a worker's `git config` changes only that clone, never the main checkout or another job;
- copies the job clone's `.git/config` at prepare, and before every git command it runs in the clone (status, diff, merge, commit, push, fetch) compares `.git/config`, and `.git/config.worktree` when present, with that copy. A difference counts as a protected violation: prelaunch_protected_failed before a launch (row 43p), protected_change at the gate (row 25), and clone_config_changed after a stage. A post-stage difference is a failed post-stage check, and rows 43x (stage_failed) and 43y (lease_expired) send it straight to needs_human, ahead of rows 39 and 39d, which would snapshot, reset or relaunch in the clone. On that entry the engine does not abort a merge in progress either. No engine git command runs in that clone until a person restores the config from the prepare copy, which status prints how to do;
- runs every git command, in the job clone and in the main checkout, with `-c core.hooksPath=<empty dir> -c core.fsmonitor=false`, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL set to the engine's own file, and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 (with `-c core.fsmonitor=false`, `git status` did not run a planted fsmonitor in git 2.55.0, checked 2026-11-11);
- reads gate.commands, bootstrap, the protected sets and every other base-ref setting from the main checkout's `origin/<base>` after its own fetch before every launch and every gate, never from a ref in the job clone, so a worker's `git update-ref` cannot choose them.

P15 checks this. A deliberate same-user write to the main checkout's `.git/config` is not covered; residual_risks states it.
- **launchd or cron:** the plist environment; P13 checks it.

**Cleanup**

No force removal, no local branch deletion, and the remote branch is kept on reject.

**tier-gate additions**

The factory rules live in a separate hooks/scripts/lib/tier-factory.sh. tier-gate.sh sources it only when a FLOW_FACTORY_* variable is set in its own environment or the resolved factory directory `<main checkout>/<runtime dir>/factory/` exists. Otherwise none of the rules below runs, so ordinary flow runs in other repositories are unaffected.
1. **Worker sessions** (FLOW_FACTORY_JOB or FLOW_FACTORY_DIRECTIVE in the hook's own environment): allow exactly `flow-factory.sh context --mode` and `flow-factory.sh await <qid> [--max-seconds <n>]`, and deny every other Bash command naming flow-factory.sh or _flow_factory.py (person_channels item 2).
2. **Other sessions:**
   - confirm, approve-spec, feedback, rework, retry, reject, cancel and rebuild, and `answer` with `--text`: in default permission mode they always ask, showing the command with its arguments (for confirm, the literal and its sha256 from the read-only `flow-factory.sh status --intent <intent>`); in any other mode, or with no mode in the hook input, they are denied (person_channels item 3);
   - `answer` without `--text`, next, wait, question, status and probe are not tiered;
   - Bash commands that name the resolved absolute factory directory are denied, so a command such as `ls src/outbox/` in another project is not;
   - when flow.factory.enabled is true for the repository, Bash commands that post an issue or PR comment (`gh issue comment`, `gh pr comment`, `gh api` to a comments or reviews endpoint) and name `/flow-factory` are denied, so a session cannot post a person command as the person through ordinary tool calls. Like every text match, this does not stop a body built at run time or read from a file; nothing else stops it, and the user accepted that risk on 2026-11-12 (person_channels item 5, residual_risks). Write, Edit and NotebookEdit under the factory directory are denied by the separate factory-state-guard.sh hook (person_channels item 4);
   - e2e-tier-gate asserts that tier-gate's always-ask list equals the Person group of person_channels item 1 as `flow-factory.sh` prints it in its usage text, so adding or renaming a person subcommand fails the test until both agree.
3. **Phase 2:** `flow-factory.sh run` without `--no-merge` is classified as merge.

**Workers** write files only, with the disallowed prefixes `git push`, `gh api`, `gh issue create|comment|edit|close` and `gh pr create|comment|review|edit|ready|close|merge|checkout`. These are best-effort (P10). The launcher passes workers none of the person's GitHub tokens; worker_github_access says what a worker can still reach.

**How the engine applies tiers**

The engine calls the real gh and git and applies each key itself. It takes the strictest value of four sources: the base-ref project file, the main checkout's local file, the user tier and the plugin default. tier-gate resolves the same key differently: cascade-resolve.sh takes the first source that has a value. With project=confirm and local=autonomous, an ordinary /flow:pr push runs autonomously while the factory parks the same push for a confirm. three-tier-safety.md states the difference.
- autonomous: run;
- journal: run, plus one breadcrumb through bin/flow-tier-crumb.sh;
- confirm: see below.

**Writes each stage makes**

| Stage | Blocking writes | Notices |
|---|---|---|
| intake | none | comment and labels |
| prepare | assignment (issueAssign) and label (issueUpdate) | none |
| open_pr | push; pr create (prCreate) or pr edit (issueUpdate) | none |
| review | push; review marker and resolution marker (issueUpdate) | none |
| rework | push; resolution marker; replies | none |
| sync and resolve | push | none |
| ready | pr ready and label | summary |
| leaving ready | pr ready --undo and label | none |
| parked states and reject | none | comment and label; pr close on reject |

**When a key is confirm**
- **Before launch (row 40b).** If any blocking key left on the job's path is confirm and the executor cannot confirm at write time, the job parks in waiting_operator with reason `tier_confirm` before any judge, worker or bootstrap spend. With headless runner and tiers.push=confirm, a job no longer spends spec and build budget (defaults $5 + $20) only to park at the push. Exits: row 41b when the key no longer resolves to confirm, and row 41p when an interactive executor that can confirm (one in default permission mode; in auto mode none can) picks the job up.
- **At write time (row 40).** A blocking write with no confirmation goes to waiting_operator with pending_intent. Exits: row 41 on a confirm, row 41e when the effect is observed, row 41k when the key changed and the engine ran the write.
- **Leaving ready (rows 40g, 40p, 40f and 40r) and the phase 2 states (rows 40, 40f, 40g, 40j, 40l, 40p, 40t, 40x and 40y).** The undo of ready is a blocking write, so a move out of a state where the PR is marked ready to a non-terminal state parks the job the same way when its key is confirm. After the confirm the job resumes into ready, and a held github_change, rework or feedback is replayed there. Row 40g covers every github_change that would move such a job.
- **Which writes a row makes** is data: each row of transitions.json lists its blocking writes in `writes`, and blocking_write_confirm is true only when the row that would apply lists one whose key is confirm.
- **Notices** stay `pending_confirm` and never block.
- **Interactive executor.** In default permission mode it runs `flow-factory.sh confirm <intent>` (id only), and tier-gate's ask, which shows the literal, is the confirmation. In auto mode the job parks before launch, and a person confirms in a terminal (person_channels items 3 and 4).
- **Headless runner.** Pending items are listed in status and runner.log. A person can confirm in a terminal, run the literal, or change the key. setup and probe warn when issueUpdate is confirm.

**Documentation.** three-tier-safety.md states that the engine deliberately runs the real binaries, and that it applies the same keys itself, including the pre-launch park.

**Tier 3** is unchanged in every session. Phase 2 adds only the runner exception.

__open_before_fix: Advisor directive: check the Tier 2 confirm settings before launch and park in waiting_operator. -- The design only parks when a blocking write is the next step (row 40). The directive asks for the check before launch. [In the design, row 40's guard is 'the next step is a blocking write whose key resolves to confirm', and github_writes_and_tiers puts the check at write time. No pre-launch tier check appears in the prepare guard (row 11), in execution_model's `next`, or in setup/probe, which only warn when issueUpdate is confirm.]

User decision 5: the interactive executor in which 'the session drives jobs and asks questions immediately'. -- The design says this is open. Reading A (engine-spawned `claude -p` workers, with the session asking only after a worker has stored its question and stopped) is a recommendation. The user still has to answer through AskUserQuestion before phase 1c. [interactive_executor, 'Decision 5 is open for the user'; phasing, 'Before phase 1c'; residual_risks, last item.]

Advisor directive: Phase 0 probes are go/no-go and include `gh pr review` on one's own PR, and push plus `gh pr create` under the cleaned environment. -- P6 (own-PR `gh pr review --comment`, the author_association it gets, and the CI effect of `gh pr ready`/`--undo`) and the GitHub-writing part of P3 are deferred to the approved live run in phase 1h. By then the marker and ledger design (1f) and the ready/undo logic (1g) are already built. So these are not go/no-go gates before the work that depends on them. Fallbacks exist, but the order defeats the 'go/no-go first' intent. The user's approval for a sandbox write could be asked for at phase 0 instead. [In the design, phasing Phase 0: 'P6 and the GitHub-writing part of P3 run only in the approved live run'. Probe P6: 'Approved live run only'.]

Workers can approve their own spec through the engine's command line. `flow-factory.sh approve-spec`, `answer`, `retry`, `reject` and `cancel` are the channels a person uses, but nothing tells a person's call apart from a worker's. tier-gate is changed to always ask only for `confirm`, and a worker has Bash plus the plugin's bin path (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT). A prompt-injected or confused worker can run `flow-factory.sh approve-spec <job> --spec-hash <h>` and get past decision 4's spec-approval park (rows 15 and 23b), or answer its own blocking question. Possible fixes: these subcommands refuse when FLOW_FACTORY_JOB, FLOW_FACTORY_DIRECTIVE or FLOW_FACTORY_IO is set or a claude process is among the caller's ancestors (P12's method); or tier-gate always asks for them, and they are disallowed in workers. (Design: execution_model subcommand list; github_writes_and_tiers 'tier-gate classifications added' covers only confirm; the runner section treats the command line as a person's approval.)

A stale specification journal is reused when an issue is queued again. The journal is tracked and reaches base: `git ls-files .decisions` at aab0d132 lists issue-101.md, issue-110.md and issue-111.md. In factory mode, specification-capture Step 1 skips the staleness rule and returns the four elements unchanged when they are present. For a reopened or re-queued issue whose earlier PR merged, the spec stage therefore reuses the old `## Specification`. Intake's new scope and non-goals never reach it, and spec_hash is recorded over the old text. The per-job goal id (issue-N-f<k>) fixed this collision for goals but not for the journal. Separately, start.md:550 still prints `GOAL_LINK=issue-$ISSUE_NUM` into the FlowRun record, which points the run at the base goal id rather than the job's FLOW_FACTORY_GOAL_ID.

An outsider can park any ready PR. Row 38 and the ready guard require that the latest review and resolution markers on the PR, 'by any author', are engine-posted. On a public repository, anyone can post an issue comment containing `<!-- FLOW_RESOLUTION_CYCLE:N ` and move a ready job to needs_human. /flow:merge filters markers by author_association (merge.md:185-186 select the markers, then 314-346 apply the trust list). The factory's agreement check should ignore untrusted markers the same way instead of escalating on them. (Design: review_routing_and_markers item 5; row 38.)

Ordinary discussion by trusted people parks jobs. issue_digest covers every trusted comment except engine-marked and command comments. A teammate's comment on the issue after build began (a status note, 'thanks', a link) therefore makes issue_changed true and sends the job to needs_human through row 51. Before build, the same comment sends it back to intake through row 50. The design's own E2E test asserts that 'a trusted human comment does change it'. The job is parked even though nothing about the requirements changed. Options: only body and title edits move the digest, plus comments a person marks as spec input; or a judge decides whether a comment changes scope.

Rows 18 and 50 overlap. Both move needs_spec_approval with resume_state build to intake on issue_changed, and row 50 also kills a live worker. The two rows are duplicate authorities in the 'only authority' table, and the doc-equals-engine test cannot tell which one is meant.

Row 37 lets ready move to rework on a trusted `/flow-factory retry <text>` as well as on a trusted CHANGES_REQUESTED review. The directive said 'ready->rework only on trusted CHANGES_REQUESTED'. The extra trigger is trusted, but the design does not record it as a deliberate departure from the directive.

Severity high. The worktree-cleanliness guards still fail by default in target repositories. Moving the io files out of the worktree and adding runs/.gitignore does not fix this, because flow's own lock files dirty the tree. -- journal-append.sh and flow-goal-record.sh leave `<journal dir>/issue-N.md.lock` and `<runtime dir>/goals/<id>.goal.yaml.lock` beside the files they write. /flow:setup does not ignore either one. This repository hides the problem only because its own .gitignore lists both patterns. Fix: prepare writes ignore rules for `<journal dir>/*.lock` and `<runtime dir>/goals/*.lock` (for example in .git/info/exclude of the worktree), or the finalize rule and the clean-tree guards exclude *.lock. critic.wrong[9] (portability) is only partly closed. The recorded interpreter is 'the first python3 on PATH', and on this Mac that is a pyenv shim, not an interpreter. -- `command -v python3` gives ~/.pyenv/shims/python3. That file is a bash script that runs `pyenv exec python3`, and pyenv picks the version from PYENV_VERSION or a .python-version file in the working directory or its parents. The gate and bootstrap run with cwd = the worktree, so a branch that commits .python-version chooses the engine's interpreter (reasoned from pyenv's documented behaviour). Under launchd the shim also needs pyenv and bash on PATH. P11 runs from a terminal cwd and would pass anyway. Fix: probe records `sys.executable` from the resolved interpreter, refuses paths under a shims directory, and P11 and P13 run the recorded path with cwd = a worktree. [Verified 2026-11-11: `command -v python3` gives /Users/danielbentes/.pyenv/shims/python3. The shim body is `exec "/opt/homebrew/opt/pyenv/bin/pyenv" exec "$program" "$@"`. `python3 -E -c 'import yaml'` resolves to ~/.local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/yaml. /usr/bin/python3 -E cannot import yaml.]

Severity medium (reasoned). probes.json is keyed by `claude --version`, and the engine 'refuses to launch without a passing record for the current version'. Each update would make a headless runner stop launching mid-drain until P1-P5, P7-P11 and P13 run again, and some of those cost money or need a launchd run. The design needs a rule for which probes must re-run on a version change, and what the runner does meanwhile: park the jobs and record a status line.
